title: dedicated-autoscaler: fix burst util reporting and add smoothing + telemetry
author: Maya Chen
description:
Context: customers running Dedicated fleets observed sporadic spikes in reported burst utilization which didn't match observed token consumption. Root cause: the burst utilization reporter double-counted short-lived token allocations when a request moved between queue slots during fast preemption, and the tokenbucket smoothing didn't account for sub-second allocation bursts. This caused misleading dashboards and automated autoscaler decisions (ENG-1532).

What this PR does: - Fixes double-counting in the burst util reporter by tagging allocations with a unique allocation_id and deduplicating allocations seen within the same metrics interval. - Adds a small exponential smoothing window in the Dedicated autoscaler tokenbucket accounting to stabilize short sub-second bursts (configurable via feature flag: dedicated.autoscaler.burst_smoothing_enabled, default: true). - Emits two new telemetry metrics: dedicated.burst_tokens_used (per-fleet) and dedicated.burst_capacity_allocated to improve observability and alerting thresholds. - Adds unit + integration tests covering the allocation lifecycle and a new e2e telemetry test that validates reported metrics against simulated request traces. - Updates the observability docs and Grafana dashboard panels to surface the new metrics and explain the smoothing behavior.

Files changed (high level): see changed_files list.

Testing and CI: - Ran full unit and integration suite locally and in CI. First CI run failed due to a race in TestTokenBucket when the test was asserting metrics immediately after allocation; fixed by adding a small retry/assert-with-timeout and mutex around internal metrics map (commit message below). Integration tests and e2e telemetry tests passed on re-run.

Rollout notes: - Default smoothing flag is enabled; behavior is backwards compatible (no breaking API changes). Ops can disable via config for canary fleets if needed. Dashboards updated; recommend a canary rollout to a single dedicated fleet for 48h before broad rollout.

Related: ENG-1532, OPS-478, SUP-8921.
